title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Business Registries Stabilisation and Uplift) Bill 2026
short_title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Business Registries Stabilisation and Uplift) Bill 2026

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would strengthen director identification requirements and give the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) broader powers to administer company and business registers.
Directors would provide their identification numbers to companies, which would report them during registration and updates, while new powers would support publication and correction of information.
New director number reporting duties would begin on 1 July 2027, while the bill would also prevent commencement of superseded business register modernisation legislation.
changes: ASIC could disqualify directors for up to three years for failing to apply for a number when directed, subject to notice and hearing safeguards.
Company officers could nominate an alternative Australian service address while still supplying their residential address to ASIC.
ASIC could deregister a company if it had reason to believe the company supplied materially incomplete, misleading, false or deceptive information.
The Registrar's infringement notice power would be repealed, leaving ASIC as the intended sole enforcement agency for director numbers.
summary.affected: Directors, company officers, companies, other registrable bodies, ASIC and the business registers Registrar are affected.

speeches.speaker: Karen Grogan
speeches.brief: Presented Selection of Bills Committee Report No. 6 of 2026, recommending immediate referrals of four bills to legislative committees with reporting dates from 17 June to 6 August 2026. Moved amendments referring the National Disability Insurance Scheme Amendment (Securing the NDIS for Future Generations) Bill 2026 to inquiry and excluding the Competition and Consumer Amendment (Responding to Exceptional Circumstances) Bill 2026 from referral.

speeches.speaker: Joanne Ryan
speeches.brief: Declared that Appropriation Bill (No. 1) 2026-2027, Appropriation Bill (No. 2) 2026-2027 and Appropriation (Parliamentary Departments) Bill (No. 1) 2026-2027 stood referred to the Federation Chamber immediately, with Treasury Laws Amendment (Business Registries Stabilisation and Uplift) Bill 2026 referred at the adjournment of its second reading debate.

speeches.speaker: Kevin Hogan
speeches.brief: Supported the Treasury Laws Amendment (Business Registries Stabilisation and Uplift) Bill 2026 and said the coalition would not oppose it in the House so a Senate inquiry could examine director ID privacy protections, strict liability offences and ASIC's regulatory direction.

speeches.speaker: Jo Briskey
speeches.brief: Argued that the bill would prevent legacy provisions from transferring business registry responsibility from ASIC to a body created for a cancelled program, support ASIC's digital and registry powers, protect directors' addresses, link director IDs to company records, and keep RegistryConnect on track.
